BEFORE  HONOURABLE MRS. JUSTICE MITALI THAKURIA  ORDER 15.07.2024 Heard Mr. S. M. Abdullah P., learned counsel for the petitioners.

Also heard Mr. K. K.
Parasar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State respondent.
This application filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, praying for setting aside and quashing of the impugned Complaint Case No.139/2024 registered under Sections 120(B)/420/294/506 of IPC pending before the Court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Bilasipara and the impugned cognizance Order dated 09.04.2024.
Page No.# 3/4 Issue notice to the respondents, returnable within 3 (three) weeks.

Since Mr. Parasar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, has entered appearance and accepted notice on behalf of the State respondent No. 1, no formal notice is required to be issued to the said respondent.
However, he shall be provided with requisite extra-copy of the petition, if not already served, during the course of the day.
The learned counsel for the petitioners shall take steps for service of notice upon respondent No. 2 by registered post with A/D as well as by usual process within a week from today.
Also, call for the scanned copy of the LCR from the learned Court below.

Mr. Abdullah P., learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the accused/petitioners are the employees under Assam Power Distribution Company Ltd. (in short 'APDCL') who are presently posted at Chapor Electrical Sub-Division and they have performed their duty by disconnecting the electricity connection in regard to default of payment made by the complainant.

It is contended by the petitioners that the complainant had defaulted to make payment of an amount of Rs. 32,136/-
(Rupees Thirty-two thousand one hundred thirty-six) only to APDCL, Chapor Electrical Sub-Division against the consumption of energy since last September' 2023 to February' 2024.

As per last bill dated 19.02.2024, the complainant has consumed total 3145 Units of electricity against which payable amount is of Rs.22,886/- (Twenty-two thousand eight hundred eighty-six) only in addition to an arrear amount of Rs. 2879/- (Rupees Two thousand seventy-nine) only.
Thus, the outstanding payable amount becomes Rs.32,136/- (Rupees Thirty-two thousand one Page No.# 4/4 hundred thirty-six) only as on 19 th February, 2024.
Thus, only on the ground of disconnection of the electricity connection, the complainant lodged the FIR against the present petitioners with some false and concocted allegation.

More so, he submits that the petitioners are employed at the time of commission of offence with the affairs of the State Government, so it is the mandate of law that prosecution sanction be needed prior to summoning the present petitioners, but, no prosecution sanction has been obtained in the present case prior to taking cognizance of offence vide order dated 09.04.2024 and as such the impugned order dated 09.04.2024 is liable to be set aside and quashed.

He further submitted that the power company has the statutory right to disconnect the electrical connection of a consumer on a valid reason of being defaulter of payment of energy charges and hence, in the instant case also the complainant had filed the Complaint Case No.139/2024 which itself is not maintainable and thus,
he prays for stay of the aforesaid proceedings, till disposal of the instant criminal petition.

Considering the submissions of learned counsels of both sides, further proceedings of the impugned Complaint Case No.139/2024 registered under Sections 120(B)/420/294/506 of IPC pending before the Court of learned Sub- Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Bilasipara and the impugned cognizance Order dated 09.04.2024, stands stayed, till disposal of the instant criminal petition.
List the matter after 3 (three) weeks.
